- Model consistently overestimates prices in the short term (first 5–10 days) after sentiment spikes (positive sentiment > 0.2), especially when recent history shows upward momentum.
- After a sentiment dip (negative sentiment > -0.16), model tends to overshoot downward, then corrects — but often lags by 2–3 days, leading to persistent underestimation in the middle-to-late forecast horizon.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, model exhibits mean-reversion bias: forecasts too high early, then too low late, failing to capture gradual decline.
- Overshoots after sharp sentiment upturns (e.g., +0.61) are common in 30-day forecasts — model reacts too aggressively, then corrects with a lag, causing overcorrection in later days.
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., -0.16 or lower) — especially in the 10–20 day window — suggesting it underweights negative sentiment signals.
- Horizon-specific: 1–5 day forecasts are often too high, 15–30 day forecasts are too low unless sentiment is strongly positive.
